name: job-posting-section
purpose: The body of a careers posting page, under the posting's title band: the description in rows, one per section of the posting (a heading, then its paragraphs and bullet lists), beside a sticky rail that restates the posting (its area, its title and its facets such as department, location and contract) with the link to the application; then the application form, and a dialog that confirms a sent application with a way back to the open positions. From the design sample's careers job page. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'job-posting-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `module`, `registration-frame`, `module-header`, `eyebrow`, `button`, `field`, `label`, `input`, `phone-input`, `file-dropzone`, `file-token-group`, `alert`, `dialog` and `panel`. It collects data, so it follows the forms exception of the page-section contract: it validates on submit only and emits `submit`; the site sends the application and hands the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.
useWhen: On the page of one open position, under a `hero-section` (`variant: 'title-band'`) that carries the posting's title and its apply link.
avoidWhen: For the list of open positions → use `listing-index-section`.
For a lead or contact form at the top of a landing page → use `hero-form-section`.
For a newsletter sign-up at the end of a page → use `newsletter-section`.
related: `hero-section` — the title band above the posting; its action links to `#` plus `form.anchor`.
`hero-form-section` — the sibling page section that also emits `submit` and takes `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.
bestPractices: Write each section as a short heading and its `blocks`: a `text` block per paragraph, a `list` block per bullet list, in the posting's order.
Keep `facets` to the four the listing states (department, location, work arrangement, contract), each with a glyph.
Set `form.anchor` (for example `apply`) and point the title band's action at `#apply`; the rail's apply button links there too.
Put the format and size limits of a `file` field in its `helper`, and the accepted types in `accept`.
Mark only what the team needs as `required`; say "Optional." in the `helper` of the rest.
Send the application from the `submit` handler, read the file from `new FormData(event.target)`, and set `loading`, then `submitted` or `failed`.

props.name: form
props.doc: The application form: `{ title, description?, submitLabel, anchor?, ariaLabel?, fields }`, where `anchor` is the id of the apply section the rail button links to and a field is `{ name, type, label, required?, helper?, placeholder?, accept?, autocomplete?, country? }`.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Copy of the form and its outcomes: `{ missing, invalidEmail, invalidUrl, error, successTitle, successDescription, done, browse }`.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: area
props.doc: Area the posting is filed under, the overline of the rail.

props.name: title
props.doc: Title of the posting, restated at the top of the rail; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: facets
props.doc: Facts about the posting listed in the rail, in order; each is `{ label, icon? }`.

props.name: applyLabel
props.doc: Label of the rail button that links to the application form; the button is left out when empty.

props.name: sections
props.doc: The description, one row per section in order; each is `{ title, blocks }` where a block is `{ variant: 'text', text }` or `{ type: 'list', items }`.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: Link in the confirmation dialog back to the open positions; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The site is sending the application: the submit button shows its loading state, every control is disabled and a submit is ignored.

props.name: submitted
props.doc: The site sent the application: the confirmation dialog opens.

props.name: failed
props.doc: The site could not send the application: `messages.error` shows under the submit button.
